CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual examination

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a significant past medical history of coronary artery disease status post prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc presenting for her annual exam. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well following a steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel symptoms have also resolved since surgical release a couple of years ago; she has returned to work with full range of motion and no numbness or tingling. Over the last month, she has been experiencing chest pain characterized as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest. The pain occurs with ambulation and resolves with rest, but does not occur at rest. She reports the pain occurs approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She has also noticed some nasal congestion attributed to seasonal allergies and pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pain with exertion and nasal congestion. Negative for shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Herniated disc status post steroid injection
Carpal tunnel syndrome status post release

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol
Crestor 20 mg once daily (newly started)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Employed, currently working full duty

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygen saturation normal
Cardiovascular: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Carotid: No bruits appreciated
Extremities: No lower extremity edema; healed surgical scars noted on right wrist
General: Well-appearing

RESULTS
Echocardiogram (prior year): Left ventricular ejection fraction 45% with mild mitral regurgitation
EKG: Stable, consistent with prior coronary artery disease, no new changes

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel syndrome status post release: Patient doing well with full recovery and return to work. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient instructed to report any recurring symptoms.

2. Herniated disc: Doing well with prior steroid injection. No current limitations. No further steroid injection or physical therapy indicated at this time. Patient instructed to report any recurrent symptoms.

3. Coronary artery disease with exertional chest pain: Patient to continue aspirin and Toprol. Started on Crestor 20 mg once daily. Cardiac stress test ordered to evaluate for additional coronary blockages. Lipid panel ordered. Follow-up pending stress test results.
